featureRef: 29.7 Working the pickup queue and releasing a child
name: Show who is waiting, send the child, and record that they left and when — the only record of a child leaving during the day
priorityReason: Nothing else in the system records a student leaving the premises during the day, and this is the record the school needs if a collection is ever questioned.

goal.actor: a Coordinator and the staff at the gate
goal.capability: to see who is waiting, send the child, and record the handover
goal.outcome: the child reaches the right gate, the guardian is not left waiting, and the school has a record that the child left

secondaryActors.involvement: Confirms the handover at the gate and records it.
Sees requests that have aged, and reviews the collection record.
Is told so the child can leave the lesson.

additional.description: A request is raised by geofence, pickup card or gate barcode.
A request ages beyond the configured minutes and is escalated (BR-7).
The window closes with a request never completed, which is recorded as not collected (BR-9).

preconditions.condition: A pickup request has been raised by one of the three routes.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is a Coordinator or gate staff.
The coordinator's own WhatsApp numbers are recorded, since the message goes to them (BR-2).
The escalation period and the end of the window are configured (BR-7, BR-9).

postConditions: Open requests appeared in a queue on the coordinator's dashboard with the student, the section, how the request was raised, and how long it had been waiting.
A WhatsApp message went at the same time to the coordinator's own numbers, since neither they nor the teacher is watching a screen while teaching.
The message went to those individuals and not to the section's parent group, which cannot receive one from the Business API and where it would tell thirty families when one child leaves.
The message pointed at the queue and was not the record itself.
The child was sent to the gate and handed over to whoever raised the request.

The handover was recorded with the child, the time and the branch. There was no authorised-collector list to check against, so what is recorded is that the child was released against this request rather than who took them.
Where the staff member had any doubt, the child was not released and the School Admin was called. The system could not refuse it, so the judgement rested with whoever was on duty.
The request was marked completed from the queue in one action, which is the record that the child left and when.
A request open beyond the configured minutes was escalated and appeared on the School Admin's screen.
An early collection recorded its reason and marked the attendance for that day as an early departure rather than a full day present.
A request never completed expired at the end of the window and was recorded as not collected.

businessRules.rule: Open pickup requests appear in a queue on the coordinator's dashboard, showing the student, the section, how the request was raised, and how long it has been waiting.

A WhatsApp message is sent at the same time to the coordinator's own numbers, using a pre-approved template naming the student, since neither the coordinator nor the teacher is watching a screen while teaching.

The message points at the queue and is not the record itself. It is sent to those individuals and not to the section's parent group, which cannot receive a message from the Business API and where it would tell thirty families when one child leaves and who collects them.

The staff member at the gate hands the child over to whoever raised the request, and the handover is recorded with the child, the time and the branch. There is no authorised-collector list to check against, so what is recorded is that the child was released against this request rather than who took them.

Where the staff member has any doubt about the person collecting, the child is not released and the School Admin is called. The system cannot refuse this on its own, because it holds no list of who may collect, so the judgement rests with whoever is on duty.
The request is marked completed from the queue, which is the record that the child left and when. It is one action on a request already on screen and is not a separate screen.

A request open beyond a configured number of minutes is escalated, being notified a second time and appearing on the School Admin's screen, so that a guardian is not left at the gate while the coordinator is mid-lesson.
Where the collection is early, before the normal end of the day, the reason is recorded and the attendance record for that day is marked as an early departure rather than left as a full day present.
A request never completed expires at the end of the window and is recorded as not collected, so that a request raised and abandoned is visible rather than silently lost.

The collection record is retained and is readable by the School Admin and the Principal. Nothing else in the system records a student leaving the premises during the day, and this is the record the school needs if a collection is ever questioned.
A request is never deleted, and neither is a collection record or a refusal.

departures.aspect: The queue is the record, the message is not
departures.requirement: The WhatsApp message points at the queue. A failed message never loses a request, since the queue holds it.
No pickup message is sent to a section's parent group by any route. The group cannot receive one from the Business API, and it would tell thirty families when one child leaves.

departures.aspect: The system cannot refuse a release
departures.requirement: There is no list of authorised collectors, so the system cannot judge whether the right person is at the gate. The judgement rests with whoever is on duty, and this is a stated consequence of the card design rather than an omission.
Marking a request completed is a single action on a request already on screen, since a second screen is what stops it being done at the gate.
A request never completed is recorded as not collected at the end of the window, rather than disappearing.
Collection records are retained 7 years, since nothing else records a student leaving the premises during the day.

openQuestions.question: After how many minutes is a request escalated, and what is the end of the window?
What is the normal end of the day, against which a collection counts as early?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it decides whether an attendance mark changes.

openQuestions.question: The system cannot refuse a release, because it holds no list of who may collect. Where the staff member has doubts, the School Admin is called — but nothing records the outcome of that call.
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled as a refusal note. The escalation path beyond it is not specified.

openQuestions.question: A child collected mid-morning by an adult who did not raise a request is recorded nowhere, and this feature cannot capture it.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved, and it is the highest-risk event at a school gate.

openQuestions.question: Is the guardian told when the child has been released, and by which channel?
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled as a WhatsApp message. Not stated in the document.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
